recipe.title: MFASS v2 corrected k-mer and position baseline on CPU
recipe.summary: Prepares the MFASS v2 protocol from the two published MFASS tables, fits the registered k-mer and position baseline on the training split and scores the 8,324 held-out variants.

licence.weights: No pretrained weights; the baseline is fitted on the training split.
licence.data: Reuse terms are unreported upstream (KosuriLab/MFASS). The data is fetched, not redistributed.

missing.note: No rewirebench image is published. CI builds containers/Containerfile without pushing it.
No linux/arm64 image has been built.

hardware_floor.note: CPU only. Measured on 2026-11-20 on an Apple M4 (macOS arm64) by this recipe: 21.6 seconds including the input download, peak resident memory 0.83 GB. Disk was not measured; the two inputs total 80 MB.

expected_output.description: The corrected baseline values published in benchmarks/mfass/README.md, on all 8,324 held-out variants with 315 positives.

weights_pin.note: The baseline uses no pretrained weights.

estimate.note: No GPU and no paid compute.

limitations: A rerun with the project's own code and data, not an independent reproduction by another group.
Runs in the host Python environment because no container image is published yet.

results.detail: code da7694213d5148c4d7fa2ac4db85c6d15077cbea, as the receipt states it. The commit is not looked up in any repository.

result.note: Verification shows the folder is consistent with its receipt and, for a recipe run, with the recipe. Nothing is signed: hardware, times and who started the run are as trustworthy as the place the folder came from, and a metric the recipe does not check can be changed together with its digests. Checked values are read again from the output files; predictions are not scored again, because the prepared data is not in the folder. The commits check reads the commit the receipt states and does not look it up.
